title: Changes in gut microbiota in the acute phase after spinal cord injury correlate with severity of the lesion
quotes: the proportions of the mucus degrader Akkermansia, as well as those of Oscillospira, Dialister, and unclassified genera of Lachnospiraceae and [Mogibacteriaceae] were reduced in the group having more severe SCI
whose relative abundance was also found to be reduced in more severe vs. less severe SCI
note: Sentences explicitly compare Akkermansia across SCI severity levels (more vs less severe), not comparing diseased to healthy controls.

title: Comparison of the effects of probiotics, rifaximin, and lactulose in the treatment of minimal hepatic encephalopathy and gut microbiota
quotes: The results showed the enrichment of Pediococcus , Selenomonas , Anaerosinus , Lactobacillus , Pseudomonas , and Bifidobacterium , and the lack of Barnesiella in MHE patients ( Figure 4A ).
This study also demonstrated that the relative abundance levels of Bacteroides and Barnesiella in intestinal microbiota were lower in MHE, while Lactobacillus had higher levels.
note: Barnesiella reported as lacking/lower in MHE patients; comparison to healthy/normal controls is implied by the use of 'lack' and 'lower' but not explicitly named in sentences.

title: Difference in gut microbial dysbiotic patterns between body-first and brain-first Parkinson's disease.
quotes: The gut microbiome in body-first PD showed a distinct profile, characterized by an increased presence of Escherichia coli and Akkermansia muciniphila, and a decreased abundance of short-chain fatty acid-producing commensal bacteria.
note: Sentence reports increased Akkermansia muciniphila in body-first PD but does not state the comparison group (whether vs healthy controls or vs brain-first PD).

title: Gut bacteria from multiple sclerosis patients modulate human T cells and exacerbate symptoms in mouse models.
quotes: Akkermansia muciniphila and Acinetobacter calcoaceticus , both increased in MS patients, induced proinflammatory responses in human peripheral blood mononuclear cells and in monocolonized mice.
note: Akkermansia muciniphila reported as 'increased in MS patients'; the comparison to healthy controls is implied by this standard epidemiological phrasing but not explicitly stated in the sentence.

title: Gut microbiota dysbiosis in male patients with chronic traumatic complete spinal cord injury
quotes: The abundance of Megamonas, Prevotella_9, [Eubacterium]_rectale_group, Dialister, and Subdoligranulum in the healthy male group was significantly higher than that in the SCI group (p 0.05, Mann–Whitney U test).
note: Explicitly compares healthy male group to SCI group with statistical test, clearly establishing Megamonas differs between healthy controls and diseased group.

title: Gut- and oral-dysbiosis differentially impact spinal- and bulbar-onset ALS, predicting ALS severity and potentially determining the location of disease onset.
quotes: The shift in oral F/B- ratio in bALS was mainly driven by a significant depletion of Veillonellaceae family ( Firmicutes phyla) along with increased abundance of Prevotellaceae family ( Bacteroidetes phyla) (Fig. 4 B).
note: Veillonellaceae reported as significantly depleted in bulbar-onset ALS, but comparison baseline is not explicitly specified (could be vs healthy controls or vs spinal-onset ALS).

title: Oral Pathobiont Streptococcus Anginosus Is Enriched in the Gut of Stroke Patients and Predicts 2-Year Cardiovascular Outcome
quotes: Streptococcus anginosus was significantly more abundant in both the saliva (median [IQR], 0.01 [0.00–0.14] vs. 0.00 [0.00–0.03], P=0.02) and gut (0.09 [0.00–0.28] vs. 0.00 [0.00–0.02], P<0.001) of the stroke patients compared with their non-stroke counterparts.
note: Explicitly compares stroke patients to non-stroke subjects with statistical testing and quantified abundance values, clearly establishing CONTROL_CONTRAST.
